questions.question:
The solution of [latex]x\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}+y=x^{4}[/latex]
  with the condition [latex]y(1)=\frac{6}{5}[/latex]
 is
questions.explanation: Given differential equation is [latex] \begin{aligned} x \frac{d y}{d x}+y &=x^{4} \\ \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}+\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) y &=x^{3} \end{aligned}[/latex] Standard form [latex] \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x}+P y=Q[/latex] where P and Q function of x only and solution is given by [latex] y(\text { I.F. })=\int Q \cdot(I F .) d x+C[/latex] where, integrating factor (I.F.)[latex] =e^{\int P d x} [/latex] [latex] \text{Here} \quad P =\frac{1}{x} \text { and } Q=x^{3} [/latex] [latex] \text { I.F. } =e^{\int \frac{1}{x} d x}=e^{\ln x}=x[/latex] Solution [latex] \quad y(x)=\int x^{3} \cdot x d x+c [/latex] [latex] y x=\frac{x^{5}}{5}+c [/latex] given condition [latex] y(1)=\frac{6}{5} [/latex] means at [latex]x=1 ; y=\frac{6}{5} [/latex] [latex] \Rightarrow \quad \frac{6}{5} \times 1=\frac{1}{5}+c [/latex] [latex] \Rightarrow \quad c=\frac{6}{5}-\frac{1}{5}=1 [/latex] Therefore [latex] y x=\frac{x^{5}}{5}+1 [/latex] [latex] \Rightarrow \quad y=\frac{x^{4}}{5}+\frac{1}{x}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Given differential equation is
[latex] \begin{aligned} x \frac{d y}{d x}+y &=x^{4} \\ \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}+\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) y &=x^{3} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Standard form
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x}+P y=Q[/latex]
where P and Q function of x only and solution is given by
[latex] y(\text { I.F. })=\int Q \cdot(I F .) d x+C[/latex]
where, integrating factor (I.F.)[latex] =e^{\int P d x} [/latex]
[latex] \text{Here} \quad P =\frac{1}{x} \text { and } Q=x^{3} [/latex]
[latex] \text { I.F. } =e^{\int \frac{1}{x} d x}=e^{\ln x}=x[/latex]
Solution [latex] \quad y(x)=\int x^{3} \cdot x d x+c [/latex]
[latex] y x=\frac{x^{5}}{5}+c [/latex]
given condition
[latex] y(1)=\frac{6}{5} [/latex]
means at [latex]x=1 ; y=\frac{6}{5} [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad \frac{6}{5} \times 1=\frac{1}{5}+c [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad c=\frac{6}{5}-\frac{1}{5}=1 [/latex]
Therefore [latex] y x=\frac{x^{5}}{5}+1 [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad y=\frac{x^{4}}{5}+\frac{1}{x}[/latex]

Swell: This defect is found on the vertical surface of a casting if the moulding sand is deformed by the hydrostatic pressure caused by the high moisture content in the sand. Wash: A low projection on the drag surface of a casting commencing near the gate is called a wash. This is caused by erosion of sand due to the high velocity jet of liquid metal in bottom gating. questions.question: Minimum shear strain in orthogonal turning with a cutting tool of zero rake angle is
questions.explanation: During orthogonal machining. Shear strain: [latex]\gamma=\cot \phi+\tan (\phi-\alpha) [/latex] Cutting tool having rake angle: [latex]\alpha=0^{\circ} [/latex] then [latex]\quad \gamma=\cot \phi+\tan \phi[/latex] For minimum value of shea [latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{d \gamma}{d \phi} &=\frac{d}{d \phi}(\cot \phi+\tan \phi)=0 \\ \frac{d \gamma}{d \phi} &=-\operatorname{cosec}^{2} \phi+\sec ^{2} \phi=0\\ -\frac{1}{\sin ^{2} \phi}+\frac{1}{\cos ^{2} \phi} &=0 \\ \Rightarrow \frac{\cos ^{2} \phi-\sin ^{2} \phi}{\cos ^{2} \phi \sin ^{2} \phi}&=0 \\ \Rightarrow \cos 2 \phi=0=\cos \frac{\pi}{2}&=\cos \frac{3 \pi}{2} \\ \Rightarrow \phi &= \frac{\pi}{4}\\ \frac{d^{2} \gamma}{d \phi^{2}}&=-2 \text{cosec} \phi \cdot(-\operatorname{cosec} \phi \cot \phi) \\ &+2\sec\phi.(\sec\phi\tan\phi)\\ \frac{d^{2} \gamma}{d \phi^{2}}&=2 \text{cosec}^{2} \phi \cot \phi+2 \sec ^{2} \phi\\ \left.\frac{d^{2} \gamma}{d \phi^{2}}\right|_{a+\phi=\frac{\pi}{4}}& \gt 0 \end{aligned}[/latex] Therefore [latex]\gamma [/latex] is minimum at [latex]\phi=\frac{\pi}{4} [/latex] Therefore minimum shear strain [latex]\gamma[/latex] is given by [latex] \begin{aligned} \gamma &=\cot \frac{\pi}{4}+\tan \frac{\pi}{4} \\ &=2^{\circ} \end{aligned}[/latex]

During orthogonal machining.
Shear strain: [latex]\gamma=\cot \phi+\tan (\phi-\alpha) [/latex]
Cutting tool having rake angle: [latex]\alpha=0^{\circ} [/latex]
then [latex]\quad \gamma=\cot \phi+\tan \phi[/latex]
For minimum value of shea
[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{d \gamma}{d \phi} &=\frac{d}{d \phi}(\cot \phi+\tan \phi)=0 \\ \frac{d \gamma}{d \phi} &=-\operatorname{cosec}^{2} \phi+\sec ^{2} \phi=0\\ -\frac{1}{\sin ^{2} \phi}+\frac{1}{\cos ^{2} \phi} &=0 \\ \Rightarrow \frac{\cos ^{2} \phi-\sin ^{2} \phi}{\cos ^{2} \phi \sin ^{2} \phi}&=0 \\ \Rightarrow \cos 2 \phi=0=\cos \frac{\pi}{2}&=\cos \frac{3 \pi}{2} \\ \Rightarrow \phi &= \frac{\pi}{4}\\ \frac{d^{2} \gamma}{d \phi^{2}}&=-2 \text{cosec} \phi \cdot(-\operatorname{cosec} \phi \cot \phi) \\ &+2\sec\phi.(\sec\phi\tan\phi)\\ \frac{d^{2} \gamma}{d \phi^{2}}&=2 \text{cosec}^{2} \phi \cot \phi+2 \sec ^{2} \phi\\ \left.\frac{d^{2} \gamma}{d \phi^{2}}\right|_{a+\phi=\frac{\pi}{4}}& \gt 0 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Therefore [latex]\gamma [/latex] is minimum at [latex]\phi=\frac{\pi}{4} [/latex]
Therefore minimum shear strain [latex]\gamma[/latex] is given by
[latex] \begin{aligned} \gamma &=\cot \frac{\pi}{4}+\tan \frac{\pi}{4} \\ &=2^{\circ} \end{aligned}[/latex]
